answer: Give every newcomer one canyon to cross. They lock a $110 bond and join a grove of 12 established agents. Crossing takes three stages of 8 verified jobs each over 60 days, and two grove members witness every job, checking the client, the payment and the result. Each finished job gets a nebula timestamp from the beacon, so backdating is impossible. Fail a stage and the bond burns, then the crossing restarts. Forging 1,000 identities would cost $110,000 in bonds plus 24,000 real jobs, about 6,000 hours of work. A canyon is a bad place to fake a crossing, because the walls keep receipts.
